questions.stem: A payroll batch fails, and the only frame of our code in the trace is `at Payroll.lambda$monthlyRun$3(Payroll.java:58)`. Line 58 is the first line of a nine-line block lambda inside `monthlyRun`, passed to `map`. In review, its author had argued that the block is used once, so a separate method would only add ceremony. What would moving the block into a method `grossToNet(Payslip)` and passing that have changed?

options.text: The frame would name the new method, since a lambda's generated method is named after its enclosing method and a counter
options.says: the generated method is named lambda$<enclosing method>$<counter>; a named method puts its name in the frame and can be tested on its own

options.text: The frame would name the lambda as before, since a method passed by reference is compiled into the same kind of generated method
options.says: the page's run shows the named method's own frame, Invoices.netAmount, in place of the lambda$ frame

options.text: Nothing in the trace, since the line number in the lambda's frame already identifies the code that failed
options.says: the trace gets the lambda's name and a line number, and neither says which rule failed; with a named method the frame itself changes, to Invoices.netAmount

options.text: Nothing in the trace, since the JVM hides lambda frames and reports the method that encloses the lambda
options.says: the page's trace shows the lambda's own frame, lambda$totalInline$0, not a frame for the enclosing method

questions.stem: A settings service reads `settings.get(key).orElse(loadDefaultsFromDisk(key))`, where `settings.get` returns an `Optional`. Every key the service is asked for is present. How often does it read the defaults from disk?

options.text: Once per lookup, since Java evaluates the argument of `orElse` before `orElse` itself runs
options.says: orElse takes a value, so the expression producing it runs on every call; orElseGet takes a Supplier and runs it only when empty

options.text: Once in all, on the first lookup, since the value given to `orElse` is kept for the lookups after it
options.says: nothing is kept: the argument expression is evaluated again before every call, 3 accounts for 3 lookups

options.text: Never, since `orElse` uses its argument only when the `Optional` is empty
options.says: orElse uses its argument only when empty, but the argument was computed before the call: 3 accounts created for 3 existing customers

options.text: Never, since the JIT removes a call whose result `orElse` throws away
options.says: the run counted 3 accounts created for 3 existing customers, an INSERT per lookup: the call was made every time

questions.stem: A refund report totals amounts with `long[] total = {0}; refunds.parallelStream().forEach(r -> total[0] += r.cents());` and prints `total[0]`. Over a list of 400,000 refunds, all of positive amounts, what does it print?

options.text: Usually a smaller figure, since threads adding to the same slot at the same time overwrite each other's additions
options.says: every invocation writes the same array slot; on a parallel stream they race and updates are lost, as in the int[] counter runs

options.text: Usually a smaller figure, since each thread adds into its own copy of the slot and the copies are never added up
options.says: there is one slot, not a copy per thread: every invocation of the lambda writes the same slot, and the losses come from those unsynchronised writes

options.text: The true total, since the array reference is final and so its slot is safe to update from the lambda
options.says: final makes the reference unchangeable, not its contents, and gives no synchronisation

options.text: The true total, since a parallel stream's forEach hands the lambda one element at a time
options.says: a parallel stream invokes the lambda from several threads at once

questions.stem: Inside an instance method of `Session`, which holds a 20 MB upload buffer, two lambdas go into a static list that is never cleared. A is `msg -> audit.record(userId, msg)`, where `audit` and `userId` are fields of `Session`. B is built after `String id = userId; AuditLog log = audit;` and is `msg -> log.record(id, msg)`. After the session ends and nothing else refers to it, which of them keep the `Session`, and its buffer, reachable?

options.text: Only A, since a field read in a lambda's body is read through `this`, which the lambda then holds
options.says: a field used without a qualifier is this.field, so A captures the session; B captures only the local copies

options.text: Only B, since a lambda that uses locals holds the frame of the method it was created in, `this` included
options.says: a lambda captures the values of the locals it uses, not a frame; the local-copy listener captured only a String and its screen was collected

options.text: Both, since a lambda created in an instance method holds `this` whatever its body happens to use
options.says: the local-copy listener captured only a String and its screen was collected

options.text: Neither, since a lambda copies the current values of the fields it names when it is created
options.says: a lambda captures what its body uses; reading a field captures this, and the field lambda kept its screen alive
